Cohort and outcome summary¶

Table 1 describes admissions rather than repeated measurements. Continuous variables use median [Q1, Q3], and categorical variables use n (%). The outcome summary reports the source outcomes and the in-hospital death distribution.

Data quality and missingness¶

The long table preserves raw values and converts the source -1 code to missing for analysis. Absence of an event row is treated as missing measurement. The six-hour maps show temporal measurement presence, while the wide-table map shows missingness after patient-level aggregation. Missingness may reflect clinical workflow and may be informative.

In [3]:

Modeling objective and AI-use statement¶

The eventual mortality model will be assessed using the smaller of sensitivity and positive predictive value, min(TP/(TP+FN), TP/(TP+FP)), which penalizes poor performance on either missed deaths or false positive alerts. The Hosmer–Lemeshow statistic will assess calibration by comparing observed and expected deaths across risk groups. No model is fitted here.

GPT/Codex assisted with project setup, interpretation of submission requirements, code drafting, debugging, and explanations of Python, Git, pixi, missingness, and clinical variables. I reviewed the generated code, checked source paths and formats, and use assertions plus reproducible outputs to inspect results. AI can accelerate iteration but may introduce incorrect assumptions or silent transformations, so the final notebook and generated tables must be reviewed against source data.
